text:
Priya (support): 🚨 I'm seeing a sudden spike of 5xx/504s from hosted inference starting ~10:15 UTC. Multiple customers reporting timeouts and failed API calls. p95 tail latency jumped from ~350ms to 3-5s. Investigating logs now, but flagging here in case this becomes a broader outage.

Alex (infra): On it. Can you paste an example request_id and a sample error from the gateway logs? Also which region/cluster?

Priya (support): One example: request_id=req_7b2f3a, region=us-west-2. Gateway log snippet: 

```
2026-03-15T10:17:02Z gateway[gw-12] ERROR request_id=req_7b2f3a route=/v1/generate status=504 msg="tail-latency timeout" queue_depth=1023 max_queue=1024 continuous_batcher.backlog=1189
2026-03-15T10:17:03Z gateway[gw-12] WARN batcher pool=continuous batch_size=32 backlog=1189 avg_wait_ms=1823
2026-03-15T10:17:04Z runtime[rt-5] INFO tenant=acme queue_wait_ms=1890 kv_cache_hits=2% exec_ms=45
```

Priya (support): We also have a customer repro curl that consistently hits a 504 within a minute: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"summarize: lorem ipsum"}' \
  -v
# response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```

Oncall Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-10315. Priority: P1. Paging oncall.

Jamal (sre): I'm seeing saturated ingress queues on gw-12 and gw-13, both in us-west-2. Continuous batcher queues are growing and not draining — backlog > 1100 for several minutes. Likely a combination of a request spike + some slow execs that prevent batching windows from completing.

Marta (runtime): Runtime traces show a subpopulation of requests with extremely long prefix lengths (avg tokens=2048) causing long execs and holding KV caches locked. kv_cache hit rate dropped to single digits which increases per-request work. Could be a customer job that suddenly started sending long sequences.

Alex (infra): Quick mitigations we can try:
- increase gateway replicas to reduce per-instance queue depth
- temporarily lower continuous_batcher.max_window_ms so batches flush sooner (reduces waiting but may cost throughput)
- enable fast-fail policy for oversized requests (reject > token_limit with 413)
- add a temporary drop-policy for non-paid/free-tenants to free capacity

Priya (support): Customer is enterprise (Acme) on hosted. Can't drop them. They've already raised alarm. Need careful mitigation.

Jamal (sre): I'll scale gateway first: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment/gateway --replicas=8` (from 4). Also bump max_queue_size on new instances via config patch: `kubectl -n prod patch configmap/gateway-config --type json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/max_queue","value":"2048"}]'`

Marta (runtime): I recommend changing batcher window config instead of max_queue - increasing max_queue pushes the problem later. Change: `continuous_batcher.max_window_ms: 40 -> 10` to force earlier flush. Pushing a new runtime config now.

Alex (infra): Rolling scale started. Watch metrics.

Support Bot: Automated metric alert: gateway_queue_depth_p95(us-west-2) = 980 -> after scale to 8 replicas = 420 (1 min later).

Priya (support): After scale, customers still see intermittent 504s but overall error rate decreased from 6% -> 1.2%. Some tail users still hit 504s.

Marta (runtime): We pushed continuous_batcher.max_window_ms=10 on runtime pool; batcher backlog dropped from 1100 -> 260 over ~90s. KV cache warmed up for hot tenants. That reduced avg_wait_ms to ~220ms.

Jamal (sre): We're seeing fewer 504s, but there's a recurring pattern: a single tenant's long-sequence jobs are monopolizing slot allocation for a subset of hosts. Need longer-term throttles per-tenant. For now, applying a per-tenant concurrent_request_limit=20 for hosted cluster to limit tail impact. Patch: `POST /admin/tenants/acme/config {"concurrent_limit":20}`

Priya (support): Reproduced locally by sending a burst of 200 long requests to /v1/generate and observed queue depth climb and >50% of requests getting 504 within 30s when limit not enforced. With concurrent_limit=20 applied, tail 95 dropped back to normal. Repro steps attached: 

1) Acquire token for test tenant
2) Run: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"<2048-token payload>"}' &
done; wait
```
3) Observe gateway metrics and 504 spike.

Alex (infra): Action log so far: scaled gateway to 8 replicas, patched continuous_batcher window to 10ms, applied per-tenant concurrent_limit=20 for hosted. Monitoring for 15m before closing.

Support Bot: Customer Acme notified: "We've applied short-term limits and scaled capacity; engineering is investigating root cause and long-term controls. We'll follow up with timeline." :mailbox_with_mail:

Marta (runtime): Root cause hypothesis: an increase in long-sequence requests from one tenant + low KV cache hit rate produced long exec times that blocked batching and caused queues to build. Continuous batching's default window allowed large cohorts to form and amplify the tail.

Jamal (sre): Next steps (owner assignments):
- Marta -> create a runtime change to add adaptive batching: reduce max_window for streams with high backlog
- Alex -> implement autoscale rule to spin gateways more quickly when queue_depth_p95 > 500
- Support/Priya -> follow up with customer for repro details and ask if they started a new job at 10:12 UTC
- Postmortem owner: Jamal (deadline EOD)

Priya (support): Customer confirmed they kicked off a large batch export job at 10:13 UTC and didn't throttle. They're okay with the temporary concurrent limit and want a plan to avoid future shared-tenant impact.

Marta (runtime): Proposed longer-term fixes: per-tenant backpressure (circuit-breaker), token-length pre-check at gateway to fast-fail oversized jobs, per-model execution class that prioritizes short interactive traffic over long-batch jobs, and improve KV cache warmup heuristics.

Alex (infra): I'll open an infra RFC for autoscale tuning and fast-path config changes.

Oncall Bot: Incident INC-2026-10315 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Jamal (sre): Closing update: error rate down to 0.4% and p95 back to baseline. Leaving it in monitoring for 2 hours then will close. Postmortem ticket: PM-2026-556 created.

Priya (support): Thanks team — will keep customer updated. I'll add the repro commands and the example request_ids to the postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
